perExplanation.evidence: Same 12px #777 text without a cover reaches the full colour: no-overlay/clean-control min 119, p05 132 (a2/results.json); live 390x844 unoccluded (scrollY 258) min 119, p05 126 (c1, c1-replay). Live desktop floor is 242 at every scroll (a2, a2-replay, c1), which matches the composite 0.9*255+0.1*119=241.4, not AA spread. The faintness reproduces in fresh renders, so the earlier crop was not the cause.

At all 3 points and all scrolls, stack[0] is h3.text-xl, position sticky, z 8, bg oklab(1 0 ~0 / 0.9), rect 310,365,819x48. It covers span.text-xs.text-gray-600 at 951,383,149x18 (stack[1]). Pixels: min=p05=242, histogram all bin 15. Fixtures match: overlay 242 vs no-overlay 119 (a2, c1). The h3 rect moves with scroll (y 365->317 for scrollY 0->48), so this is a static layout overlap, not sticking. At 390x844 the span is topmost (hintIndex 0, c1 pass 1) and renders min 119.

Broker nonDefaultAncestors is [] for the live hint in all runs (a2, a2-replay). The detector works: opacity-control lists hint-wrapper opacity 0.12 and renders min 238 (expected 238.7). The probe-reported effectiveOpacity is invalid (see invalid), but nonDefaultAncestors comes straight from the broker.

The hint rect stays fully in the viewport (y 383->335, innerHeight 900/800). Pixels are identical (min 242) at every scroll. Scrolling changes nothing at desktop. At 390 the scroll state matters only through banner occlusion (E). Scrolls >48px at desktop, where the h3 could actually stick, were not tested.

perExplanation.scope: as the cause of the faint (~242) rendering; the occlusion itself is confirmed at 390x844, scrollY 0-48
perExplanation.evidence: a2-replay/c1 at 390x844: div.fixed.bottom-0 z-[99999] bg rgb(221,236,222), rect 0,317,390x527, sits above the span (span stack index 4). uncertainties: What users perceive, and the scroll/viewport state of the original screenshot, are unknown.
Only Playwright Chromium headless at DPR 1 was tested. Firefox/WebKit, DPR>1, zoom and forced-colors were not.
Banner-dismissed state was not tested at desktop (no clicks). The banner does not cover the desktop hint, but other consent-dependent layout changes were not checked.
Widths between 390 and 1280 (md/lg breakpoints) were not tested, so the width at which the overlap starts is unknown.
Desktop scrolls beyond 48px (where the h3 may actually stick and move relative to the hint) were not tested.
Pixel stats are greyscale. The colour channels of the oklab white/0.9 composite were not checked separately (both colours are neutral, so the impact is small).
The live site may change after these runs.

renderedContrastDesktop.value: 1.12:1 (242 vs 255); theoretical composite 241.4 vs 255 = 1.125:1; supports saying ~1.1:1 for Chromium, DPR 1, 1440x900/1280x800
renderedContrastDesktop.method: WCAG relative luminance of the darkest glyph pixel (min=p01=p05=242, c1 and a2 live) against the background measured 8px above the hint (min=max=255, c1 backgroundAbove). Cross-check: unoccluded glyph cores reach exactly 119 (#777 -> 4.48:1), so the minimum is a valid proxy for the text colour.

oneLineConclusion: At desktop (1440x900, 1280x800; Chromium, DPR 1) the hint is faint (~1.12:1) because a 90%-white h3 overlaps it in the static layout. The cause is not antialiasing, ancestor opacity or scroll state. At 390x844 there is no overlap: the hint renders at #777 when unoccluded and is only hidden by the opaque cookie banner.
